items.title: Dr. Doom Is Taking Over Dave and Buster’s in Lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday
items.description: Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Dr. Doom’s latest target is entertainment chain Dave and Buster’s, which has fully submitted to the Marvel villain for an expansive Avengers: Doomsday campaign.

Starting on November 16, Dave & Buster’s is becoming Doom & Buster’s. Select locations are already rolling out ‘Doomsday Zones,’ entire sections of the arcade dedicated to the Avengers takeover. Enter the Dr. Doom archway and you’ll find a collection of Marvel games and activities in addition to new D&B drinks and prizes.

"When one of the biggest movies of the year is coming, you don't put up a poster. You bend the knee," said Jeremy Tucker, chief marketing officer at Dave & Buster's. "We gave Doom our name. We gave him the floor. We gave him the bar… All shall play."

As one of the leading arcade chains, the big tie-in is games. On Dave & Buster's floors, fans can already find a new selection of Marvel-themed activities:

Doom & Buster’s activities:

  • MARVEL Cosmic Invasion
  • Avengers: Roller Race & Battle
  • Human Crane
  • Mystery Crane
  • Thor's Hammer Strike
  • The Arena
  • Smash N Win
  • Avengers Themed Photo Booth

Cosmic Invasion is the big headliner here. The game dropped on PC and consoles last December, and through the D&B campaign, is now getting the full arcade cabinet treatment. Like the fully released version, the arcade edition will support up to four players.

We’re pretty big fans of the tag-team beat-em up, saying it "has the juice" in our 7/10 review, which knocks off some points for a limited hero gallery. Thankfully, the game has released plenty of new content in the past year. A new Doom-themed DLC, 'The Siege of Castle Doom,' is launching on November 10, and will presumably be included in the in-store activations.

New prizes vary across locations. The crane games are packed with their own range of Marvel-specific collectibles, including some vaguely described "new inflatables." Doomsday Zones will also feature a fully stocked Avengers Funko pusher, while kiosks offer new Avengers-themed prizes like Collectible Power Cards.

Throughout the campaign, ‘DOOMHOUR’ will strike at random times, offering customers double tickets on any green swipe games. D&B Rewards members will get a 24-hour heads up about the DOOMHOUR, while the rest of us peasants will simply have to wait for the alarm to blare. Registered members will also get access to new Rewards Challenges throughout the campaign.

Of course, Dave and Buster’s bars are also now serving a spread of Doom-themed drinks. For the alcohol-inclined, D&B offers the Doomsday's Dominion, Multiversal Mule, and Fantastic Flight. New mocktails include Panther's Potion and Captain’s Punch.

Marvel has been collaborating with everything from KFC to the MLB in the lead-up to Avengers: Doomsday, releasing in theaters on December 18. Dave & Buster’s, however, appears particularly willing to commit to the bit, which is exactly what Disney execs are looking for.

"Rather than creating a traditional promotion, they transformed their entire business into an immersive celebration of Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday," said Lylle Breier, EVP of Partnerships, Promotions and Events at The Walt Disney Studios. "The result is a bold, fan-first experience that extends the story beyond the theater and into the real world in a way only Dave & Buster's could."

items.title: Obsession Director Curry Barker Wants to Make a ‘F**ked Up, R-Rated’ Indiana Jones Movie
items.description: Curry Barker, famous for his hit horror flick Obsession, is keen on bringing his terrifying tastes to the world of Indiana Jones if the opportunity ever arises.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Curry Barker, famous for his hit horror movie Obsession, is keen on bringing his terrifying tastes to the world of Indiana Jones if the opportunity ever arises.

Barker shared his vision for an especially grisly take on Indy’s adventures during a conversation with Gold Derby after the outlet brought up similar remarks made by Cooper Tomlinson, Barker’s longtime collaborator who co-wrote, produced, and starred in Obsession as Ian, Bear’s best friend.

"I would want to do a really f**ked up, rated-R version of [Indiana Jones],” Barker said. “I want to do a crazy adventure movie. That's something that Cooper and I have talked about, because we feel like we've never seen something like that; we've only ever seen the family-friendly version.

“But what happens if two regular guys, or one regular guy, goes on a journey that turns crazy? Literally pushing the boundaries of that genre would be fun for me."

As previously mentioned, Tomlinson feels a similar way, hoping to bring back the action-adventure films that defined cinema through the '80s and '90s.

"I'd love to bring back the adventure epic like Raiders of the Lost Ark," he told the outlet. "What really worked with Obsession was making something that was honest and grounded in reality; obviously we can all suspend disbelief and enjoy all the crazy action stuff that isn't real. But when it comes to the characters and story, it should be more grounded and honest. That's how we're going to get those kinds of action classics back."

Speaking of action-adventure movies that defined the '90s, Michael Johnston (who played Bear in Obsession) has been cast in the next Mummy movie, which will also feature the return of Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz. Also speaking with Golden Derby, he described the contrast between filming a small-budget indie horror movie like Obsession and a grand, big-budget picture like The Mummy: Book of the Dead as “really different.”

"These productions are like a well-oiled machine; we do a scene many, many times from many, many different angles, which is nice because it gives us the opportunity to work things out. That takes the pressure off in a way," he said.

"But there's also a lot more waiting around on those sets than on indie films. With something like Obsession, you only have a couple chances to get something done, and you're also helping everyone else out behind the scenes. I'm not doing that on The Mummy; I'm sitting back in my chair and enjoying the catering. But getting to work with Brendan and Rachel is great, and [directors] Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett are the most lovely guys."

The Mummy: Book of the Dead is scheduled to release on October 15, 2027. Barker’s next movie, a horror-comedy called Anything But Ghosts, is also releasing next year in May.

items.title: The Odyssey Is Returning to IMAX Theaters in December Ahead of Awards Season
items.description: The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Odyssey is returning to theaters in December for one last hoorah before awards season goes into full swing.

Universal has announced that Christopher Nolan's R-rated epic will return to theaters on December 11 in over 1,000 cinemas across the United States and Canada. The film will be coming back to IMAX screens, including ones that support the 70MM IMAX format it was designed for. This is presumably part of a larger campaign to get The Odyssey some awards buzz ahead of the Oscars, and probably earn some extra pocket change for the studio.

The Odyssey has already made $1.8 billion at the box office to become the highest-grossing R-rated film in history. It seems hard to imagine this re-release getting it over the hump for $2 billion, as Dune Part 3 will take over premium format screens on December 18. Avengers: Doomsday will also take up as much attention for movie lovers, if not more. It's unclear if The Odyssey will continue to play on regular screens after those two movies are released, or if this is a limited one-week run.

The Odyssey is a favorite for many of the big prestigious awards, with many expecting a Best Picture nomination, Best Actor for Matt Damon, Best Director for Christopher Nolan, and many more. Whether it scores all of the nominations it's expected to get remains to be seen. It'll also be interesting to see what awards it could win, as Nolan's last film, Oppenheimer, cleaned house at the Oscars in 2023. It's rare for a filmmaker to win big twice in a row, though not unheard of. Alejandro González Iñárritu won Best Director back-to-back years in 2014 and 2015 for Birdman and The Revenant, respectively.

Nevertheless, it'll be a busy time at the movie theater in December with the return of The Odyssey and some of the year's heaviest hitters with Dune and Avengers. For those who aren't interested in venturing out into the cold to see Nolan's latest film again, The Odyssey is also coming to home video later this month.

items.title: G2 Esports Parts Ways With Head Coach Luka 'Perkz' Perković After His 'Tweet Bomb' Sparks Backlash
items.description: G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach, Luka "Perkz" Perković, following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach and retired League of Legends player Luka "Perkz" Perković following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.

The 2,676-word-long tweet was published on November 4, 2026. Perković described it as his “first and last honest post in [the] last decade,” where he could “address some things honestly.” He explained that he’d written the statement to clarify his stance on certain topics “so that, at the very least, you can hate me for what I really stand for, and then that's completely fine by me.”

In the post, which he jokingly called a “tweet bomb,” Perković said he is not a fan of and does not endorse the Tate brothers in any way; claimed that “doesn’t really do politics” and has never “ever voted once” in his life; said he is not a fan of either Donald Trump or Kamala Harris; said he is a devout Catholic; denied being a “Putin fanboy” or being on the side of Russia in the war on Ukraine; and shared his stance on abortion, comparing it to “murder.”

“I don’t really do politics, nor have I even ever voted once in my life. I do have opinions, and I wish I was more educated on the topic, but the truth is I’m not, so I stay away from it,” he wrote. “There are some things I stand for, very simple things in life, but the only thing that is unshakeable for me, how it’s so widely accepted in public, is abortion. I cannot comprehend how people do not understand that is a muder, as life is created at conception. That is one view I will die by and never change.”

Perković also addressed his relationship with retired League of Legends pro and former G2 CEO Carlos "ocelote" Rodríguez Santiago, who stepped down from the company in 2022 after sharing a video of himself at a party with Andrew Tate. “Me standing up for Carlos publicly when he was being cancelled has nothing to [do] with all the things I’m all accused of supporting. Trafficking? Misogyny? Nazism? War? Are you okay?” Perković said of the matter.

“Carlos believed in me when nobody else did. I did not have a close relationship with my family when I was 16, including my parents, [who] I was not too close with, either. …Carlos and I have gone both completely different ways. He is his own person and I’m completely my own. In the end Carlos’ ego is something that put an end to his esports career, which was f**king insane. So there is a lesson to be learned in there, as well. We have a lot of different views on life.”

Perhaps the biggest takeaway from Perković’s post was his stance on abortion. This particular remark was a main talking point among fans and fellow players on social media, sparking a massive wave of backlash against him. G2 Esports addressed the situation in a public post mere hours later, where they confirmed that they have parted ways with Perković due to his tweet.

Their full statement is as follows:

“Last night, like many of you, we saw the statement shared by the Head Coach of one of our teams. G2 is a diverse and international organization with different people from all around the world. While the world is complex and not everyone agrees on everything, some of the statements made last night do not align with G2's stance and values. We have fans with different cultures and personal opinions, and it is of the utmost importance to us as an organisation that we respect and uphold this diversity when representing G2. We acknowledge that this statement hurt many of our fans, and we want to apologize for it.

“As a result, we have decided to terminate our collaboration with the individual. We will now focus on rebuilding our staff and roster for the next season and ask for your patience, as we will not be able to communicate any changes until free agency officially opens. - Alban Dechelotte, CEO of G2.”

Perković has since published one other tweet — a Bible verse from Luke 6:22. “Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake,” he wrote. This post, too, has received backlash from users. Perković has not posted anything else on his account at the time of writing.

items.title: There's a 'Fifty-Fifty' Chance Godzilla Minus Zero Director Takashi Yamazaki Would Make a Godzilla Threequel
items.description: The ending of Godzilla Minus Zero leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki has crafted, but the writer/director says he's split on whether or not he'd want to come back to it.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic
items.content:
Godzilla Minus Zero writer/director Takashi Yamazaki told The Hollywood Reporter that he's "fifty-fifty" on whether or not he'd come back to make a third Godzilla film.

Extremely minor Godzilla Minus Zero spoilers ahead!

"I’m quite satisfied and happy with the current ending we have," Yakazaki said when asked about the film's ambiguous ending that leaves just enough room for a continuation of the story. "It entrusts the interpretation to the audience in terms of how they want to receive it and what they want to walk out of theaters with. That being said, if Godzilla Minus Zero is my last Godzilla film, that would make me a bit sad. I do have other films lined up, starting with Grandgear and a few others, but at some point in my career, I would love to revisit Godzilla and see how we can expand this world."

Grandgear was announced in 2024 as Yamazaki's first major Hollywood studio movie, with Sony Pictures, and his first English-language feature film. It's currently slated for a February 18, 2028 release. Starring Sam Nivola (The White Lotus Season 3), Nico Parker (The Last of Us, the live-action How to Train Your Dragon), and Paul Giamatti (it's Paul Giamatti...), Grandgear is a live-action sci-fi mecha movie, something Yamazaki also told THR was "something I’ve always wanted to do." Yamazaki is writing and directing, and Bad Robot is producing.

But first, Godzilla Minus Zero comes out in U.S. theaters this weekend, a mere three years after Godzilla Minus One became a box-office sensation in 2023 on a reportedly tiny $10–15 million budget and a lean 35-person VFX team, with Yamazaki overseeing. It went on to win the Oscar for Best Visual Effects, marking the first time a Japanese film took home the award, and did it with the tiniest budget of any category winner in more than a decade.

Yamazaki told IGN that, when writing Godzilla Minus Zero, he had to set aside the need to try and one-up everything he had accomplished with Godzilla Minus One. “I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place," he said. "So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.”

Godzilla Minus Zero is both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens. It's also very loud! We said it was Good in our review, calling out its "satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction."

But back to the potential of a third Godzilla movie. Turning these films into a trilogy raises a critical question: What would it be called, after the naming convention has already counted down from Minus One to Minus Zero? I have a pitch: Godzilla Plus One that, of course, introduces another new kaiju. Toho, call me!

items.title: Bethesda Is Already Selling The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Merch
items.description: Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or t-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black.

You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or T-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black.

The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel hoodie is $64.99, while the identical item in T-shirt form is $34.99. Hat tip to @MrMattyPlays on X for first spotting the Sentinel merch. Bethesda says, "Celebrate The Elder Scrolls VI. Your next journey through Tamriel will be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Show off your excitement with the official hoodie!" And if you're interesteed in ordering, note the disclaimer: "This hoodie runs small. For the perfect fit, we recommend ordering one size larger than your usual size." The T-shirt shares an identical description, minus the note about it running small.

You'll have plenty of time to break in either of these clothing items, as Sentinel isn't expected to be released for at least a couple more years. That would mean it might be at least a decade between the original announcement of The Elder Scrolls 6 and the time it's finally on your hard drive. Regardless, it's arguably the biggest game Xbox has in its portfolio by a country mile and when the release date finally arrives, it's going to be a very, very big deal.

Amidst all of the changes at Xbox this year, it will be interesting to see if, a) The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will be available on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one, b) if it might line up with the launch of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix console/gaming PC hybrid, and/or c) if it ends up being an Xbox console exclusive.

items.title: BioWare's Final Years Were Filmed and Will Be Revealed in a New Documentary
items.description: The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The last two years of BioWare's life were filmed and will be shown in a new documentary about the game studio.

The documentary, titled Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, will show the studio's journey over the last few years. While it's unclear if this will include new footage of the canceled Mass Effect game, it is a rare peek behind the curtain and likely a raw one, given how the story ends. Industry veteran Geoff Keighley revealed that he was interviewed for the film earlier this year, and confirmed that it will be released sometime in 2027.

The project is being produced by Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada‘s Super Channel, as BioWare was primarily a Canadian studio. It's unclear if it will also be made available online for those outside of Canada. The documentary will feature exclusive interviews and insights from BioWare talent, such as Mass Effect game director Casey Hudson, Jennifer Hale (voice actress for the female variant of Commander Shepard), and many more. It should be an interesting watch whenever it is released.

“When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honoured and genuinely moved,” said BioWare co-founders Dr. Ray Muzyka and Dr. Greg Zeschuk. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about deeply emotionally engaging stories and characters, brought to life by the amazingly talented people on our dev teams, and our excellent production and distribution partners who helped us bring those stories successfully to all corners of the planet, and our passionate fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honours those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.”

BioWare was shut down last month, much to the shock of the wider industry and fans alike. The studio had been struggling for a while; its last three games were misfires, and the next Mass Effect game was expected to still be years away. As a result, EA reportedly decided to place its bets on a new Star Wars Battlefront game from DICE and Respawn instead of continuing to fund a new Mass Effect game.

A trailer for Mass Effect 5, which was apparently called Mass Effect Universe, did find its way online, painting a better picture of what fans could've expected from the canceled game. Some fans have held out hope that the Mass Effect IP could be acquired by another company, but as of right now, it doesn't seem like that's in the cards.

items.title: 52-Year-Old YouTuber Learns Karate by Studying Tekken to Train With His Son
items.description: A 52-year-old Japanese YouTuber is learning karate by studying characters’ moves from Tekken after his son inspired him to pursue a journey in martial arts.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A 52-year-old Japanese YouTuber is learning karate by studying characters’ moves from Tekken 3 after his son inspired him to pursue a journey in martial arts.

AskJapan is a fairly popular YouTuber with more than 189,000 subscribers. He’s best known for his vlog-style videos where he chats with viewers and plays retro video games on old-school consoles, often while dressing up in low-budget cosplay of characters from the games he’s playing.

He’s been on a fighting game stint lately, taking on the likes of Street Fighter II and Tekken 3, the latter of which he’s using to help himself learn real-life martial arts moves. He explained this newfound interest in a November 3 video, saying one of his son’s recent karate demonstrations made him inspired to try it out for himself.

AskJapan says that his son is a brown belt, a rank that’s right beneath the black belt (the top level that signifies total mastery of the art). He’s only 10 years old, and has been training since he was 5. This fact, combined with his son’s latest “overwhelming” karate demonstration, made him want to try it out for himself. But rather than hitting the dojo first, AskJapan is taking an unconventional approach to the art; he’s taking ‘lessons’ from Tekken characters.

“His performance inspired my spirit, my motivation,” the YouTuber explained. “I thought, ‘Okay, maybe someday in the future, I [can] start karate, even though I’m 52. Why not? I realized that, to start, I have to practice karate with games. That’s why I was determined today, after watching my son’s performance this morning. Why not start today, and practice with Tekken? This is my way of improving.”

Throughout the rest of the video, he took notes from Tekken 3 as he played through the game on a homemade ‘arcade cabinet’ that he’d fashioned out of cardboard. It’s an extremely charming watch — but his second foray into the game was downright hilarious.

His next video, which he uploaded on November 4, shows him fashioning a Heihachi cosplay out of a helmet and cardboard paper. His goal was to unlock the boss character by attempting to beat Tekken 3’s arcade mode, but he unfortunately failed.

Fans are rallying behind the YouTuber on his latest mission, sharing words of encouragement for both his martial arts goals and his journey to becoming a better Tekken player.

“There is no age to start karate, and you still look in shape,” one viewer wrote.

“I hope Harada and the gang see this and appreciate it like I do,” another said, referencing the former Tekken boss.

It’s true that having martial arts experience can come in handy; earlier this year, a member of the fighting game community went viral for using skills he’d learned from sumo wrestling to fend off a knife-wielding man at his local gaming cafe. And despite the shocking ordeal, he returned to his Twitch stream straight afterward, complaining that the incident had cost him 14 LP in League of Legends.

items.title: EA Brings Every Ultima and Wing Commander Game to Steam and GOG with Quality-of-Life Updates
items.description: Electronic Arts is bringing 25 classic games from its library to Steam today, including seven Anniversary Editions for six Wing Commander games as well as Road Rash. The rest of the re-releases include every Ultima RPG, both Crusader games, Strike Commander, and Theme Hospital. The 18 re-releases are $4.99 each, while the quality-of-life-updated Anniversary Editions cost $9.99 each.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Electronic Arts is bringing 25 classic games from its library to Steam today, including seven Anniversary Editions for six Wing Commander games as well as Road Rash. The rest of the re-releases include every Ultima RPG, both Crusader games, Strike Commander, and Theme Hospital. The 18 re-releases are $4.99 each, while the quality-of-life-updated Anniversary Editions cost $9.99 each.

Regarding those quality-of-life updates, EA says that means that these refreshed versions "support modern systems, controls, improve performance and make the titles more approachable without compromising their authenticity." Regarding Wing Commander specifically, which is perhaps best remembered for its many full-motion video (FMV) cutscenes starring Mark Hamill, the companys says, "For each restored Wing Commander title, these improvements were made possible by the dedicated community, who were open and eager to collaborate with the passionate team at EA to incorporate their mods into the official releases. This launch is a celebration of the community’s commitment to the franchise, which is why anyone who already owns a digital copy of the Wing Commander titles on GOG or the EA App will automatically receive the Anniversary Edition upgrade for free on their respective digital platform."

For each of the Anniversary Editions, including my personal favorite, Road Rash (check out the trailer above), EA says, "The Anniversary Editions have been a labor of love, inspired by the discovery of a physical media vault containing thousands of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes alongside other media assets. The digitization process recovered the supposedly lost Master FMV sequences for these seven legendary titles, which were meticulously re-edited to restore the over 1,500 cinematic scenes across these games."

The Ultima series, meanwhile, was the brainchild of legendary RPG designer Richard "Lord British" Garriott, who went on to build a castle for a house and later become one of the first private citizens to go into outer space. You can hear about those stories and more on my old IGN Unfiltered interview with him from 2017.

Here's the full list of classic games EA is re-releasing:

  • Wing Commander: 35th Anniversary Edition

items.title: GOG Announces Road Rash Touch Up and a Publishing Arm for 'New Games With a Classic Soul'
items.description: GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.

The company is currently on a mission to keep games available to play even after the seasons end and servers close down. Its GOG Patrons initiative has saved 300 old games, funding them to be made compatible with modern operating systems. Over 10,000 patrons have signed up to help. The latest game to benefit from this was Nox, the action RPG developed and published by Westwood Studios and EA back in 2000.

“We dig deep into the code, fixing long-lasting bugs, adjusting screen resolutions, adding controller support, missing cutscenes and much, much more,” said Marcin Paczynski, senior business development manager.

GOG has made over 1,700 fixes to old games in its preservation program. Next up, there’s good news for classic space sim and Mark Hamill fans.

The Wing Commander series — Wing Commander 1-4 games, Prophecy Gold, and Privateer 2 — is getting an anniversary edition update. GOG collaborated with modders for Prophecy, with a goal of making the game more approachable, adding controller support to offer a new way to play.

Each of these games comes with the legacy version and the touched up Anniversary Edition. For people who already own the original games on GOG, the Anniversary Editions are free to download at launch.

Ahead of those updated space sims, there’s something new on GOG right now: Road Rash. The violent motorbike racing classic got the same treatment as Wing Commander, making it compatible with modern systems and control inputs.

GOG also announced Retro Vibe, a publishing arm focused on “new games with a classic soul.” Retro Vibe releases include a VHS-fuzzed FPS with Max Payne-esque bullet time called Cop Bastard, a side-scrolling shooter with tough boss battles called The Looter, tactical cyberpunk RPG Shardpunk 2, boomer shooter with massive boomsticks Project Warlock: Lost Chapters, and the mysterious greyscale indie game After Hell Freezes Over.

You can Wishlist the full lineup of games and check them out in more detail on GOG.com. It’s a site GOG is hoping you’ll spend more time on anyway, as the service is also introducing GOG Social, a new gaming forum integrated with your game library, allowing you to tag games in posts, taking readers directly to the store page. The forum has marked spoilers, threaded replies, reactions, post edits, media support, bookmarks, topic subscriptions, and more.

Lastly, GOG Galaxy — GOG’s launcher that lets you combine your entire library from different stores into one space — is also coming to Linux. It’s landing with new customization and personalization options. Watch the entire showcase on the GOG YouTube channel.

items.title: Wendy's RPG WendyQuest Offers Real Food Rewards for Beating Boss Fights
items.description: Wendy’s has gone full Wendy’s, releasing a 15-hour RPG based on the fast-food chain’s branding.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Wendy’s has gone full Wendy’s, releasing a 15-hour RPG based on the fast-food chain’s branding.

We were caught off guard by trailers showing some genuinely compelling turn-based gameplay, but the full launch of WendyQuest has brought yet another surprise: real rewards for beating bosses.

Every time you defeat a Mech Boss, the game will reward you with one 'Corner Stone,' which comes with a unique code. Enter the code into the 'Offers' tab on the Wendy’s app, and you’ll get a chance to win one of the following food rewards:

WendyQuest food rewards

  • FREE Medium Fry w/ purchase 
  • FREE Small Classic Frosty w/ purchase 
  • FREE 10 PC Nuggs w/ purchase 
  • FREE Biscuit or Croissant w/ purchase 
  • FREE Dave’s Single w/ purchase

There are five Mech Bosses in the game, which gives you a total of five chances to score one of the rewards. Unfortunately, repeat encounters don’t appear to net additional codes.

The rewards aren’t entirely free — to actually redeem them, you’ll have to make a "separate qualifying purchase." Classic, I know. Reward eligibility is limited to U.S. residents who are 18 and older, and players have seven days after redeeming a code in-app to complete an order before it expires.

The real-life rewards will endure "while supplies last," indicating the promotion may be time-limited. It would be kind of wild if it was a permanent fixture of the Wendy’s brand, but you never know. The company just released their third-quarter financials, reporting a 7.6% decline in U.S. systemwide sales and 5.3% decline in same-restaurant sales, and has been going all-in on the marketing stunts to try and make up some ground.

WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones launched as a free-to-play game on Steam, Android, and iOS devices on November 4, hitting a peak player count of just shy of 400 on Steam. Launching at the same time as the Ocarina of Time remake was an interesting choice, to say the least, and makes WendyQuest one of the few games releasing in the month of GTA 6.

I can’t believe you guys made a retro RPG called WendyQuest that you can download now. Oh wait that was us.

https://t.co/gEiQZ5P1P4

— Wendy’s (@Wendys) November 4, 2026


The full RPG includes around 15 hours of content, equivalent to recent AAA releases like Marvel's Wolverine. You control the red-haired Wendy, recruiting allies to stop the evil Mech Corp and save the land of Savoria.

The Mech Corp empire, under the control of Dr. MechBorg, runs with a capital 'M' logo and is all about cutting corners to earn billions, likely a direct hit at a classic Wendy’s competitor, McDonald’s. In-game abilities and items are all based on classic Wendy’s food items, with unique damage types like "Crispy," "Frosty," and "Fresh Beef."

WendyQuest was developed in collaboration with 81monkeys, a Canadian-based company, based on the 2D style of turn-based JRPG classics like Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy. As more and more games launch with full AI use disclosures, the WendyQuest Steam listing proudly proclaims the game as "100% fresh and 100% human made."

Will a solid RPG experience inspire people to eat more Wendy’s? We’ll have to see.

WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones launched as a free-to-play game on Steam, Android, and iOS devices on November 4, hitting a peak player count of just shy of 400 on Steam. Launching at the same time as the Ocarina of Time remake was an interesting choice, to say the least, and makes WendyQuest one of the few games releasing in the month of GTA 6.

I can’t believe you guys made a retro RPG called WendyQuest that you can download now. Oh wait that was us.

https://t.co/gEiQZ5P1P4

— Wendy’s (@Wendys) November 4, 2026


The full RPG includes around 15 hours of content, equivalent to recent AAA releases like Marvel's Wolverine. You control the red-haired Wendy, recruiting allies to stop the evil Mech Corp and save the land of Savoria.

The Mech Corp empire, under the control of Dr. MechBorg, runs with a capital 'M' logo and is all about cutting corners to earn billions, likely a direct hit at a classic Wendy’s competitor, McDonald’s. In-game abilities and items are all based on classic Wendy’s food items, with unique damage types like "Crispy," "Frosty," and "Fresh Beef."

WendyQuest was developed in collaboration with 81monkeys, a Canadian-based company, based on the 2D style of turn-based JRPG classics like Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy. As more and more games launch with full AI use disclosures, the WendyQuest Steam listing proudly proclaims the game as "100% fresh and 100% human made."

Will a solid RPG experience inspire people to eat more Wendy’s? We’ll have to see.

items.title: Pokémon Cards Get Official Induction Into National Toy Hall of Fame
items.description: The National Toy Hall of Fame has officially announced this year’s inductees, and the biggest TCG of all time has finally made the cut.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
The National Toy Hall of Fame has officially announced this year’s inductees, and one of the biggest trading card games of all time has finally made the cut.

Pokémon cards were inducted into the Toy Hall of Fame on the morning of Thursday, November 5, as the franchise celebrates its 30th anniversary. Other new additions from this year’s lineup include Bingo, Care Bears, and the classic slide, which beat out nominees like Bop It!, mahjong, and Polly Pocket.

"Pokémon TCG’s widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," said curator Mirek Stolee. "The Pokémon TCG successfully adapted card game formulas established by its predecessors, making it more accessible and infusing it with the lovable Pokémon creatures."

The National Toy Hall of Fame was established in 1998 to "recognize toys that have inspired creative play and enjoyed popularity over a sustained period." The Hall of Fame is currently housed at the Strong Museum of Play in Rochester, New York, which is also home to the World Video Game Hall of Fame.

Anyone can nominate a toy for consideration. A panel of museum curators, historians, and educators then evaluate these nominees based on four pillars: icon status, longevity, discovery, and innovation. The Hall of Fame has a relatively loose definition of a toy, having previously inducted a cardboard box and the concept of 'sand' in addition to classics like LEGO, Barbies, and slinkies.

This isn’t the first time a trading card game has made it onto the prestigious toy list. Magic: The Gathering was added in 2019, nearly 10 years after the induction of another tabletop classic, Dungeons & Dragons.

The Strong website now has a section dedicated to the Pokémon TCG, where it describes the game’s history and cultural impact:

"[Pokémon TCG] has played a pivotal role in popularizing the concept of trading card games and has served as an entryway into the hobby for millions. The Pokémon TCG has even spawned its own video game (for Game Boy) and app (available on multiple platforms), thus completing the circle back to its video game origins. Recently, the cards have become the focus of major financial speculation. Online viewers watch content creators “rip,” or open, TCG packs, in the hope of finding valuable, rare cards."

As of March 2026, more than 85 billion Pokémon cards have been printed and distributed globally. The trading card game is currently being printed in 13 different languages, and rough estimates put the total market cap above $15 billion.

As the museum description implies, however, the massive explosion of Pokémon’s popularity hasn’t really been a good thing for most fans. Scalping has plagued the community for years now, turning the once casual card game hobby into a collector’s racket. Market prices have soared out of control, threatening the 'accessibility' the Toy Hall of Fame specifically praises the game for.

The Pokémon Company is aware of the problem, and has repeatedly announced its intentions to increase stock to combat it. This increased production seems to have taken effect with the recent 30th anniversary product line, which led to scalpers complaining the set isn't profitable enough.

As for the Hall of Fame, Pokémon’s induction will likely lead to new exhibits and events at The Strong in the new year.

items.title: Rapper Kodak Black Will Be an NPC in GTA 6, Creating Speculation Over Other Artists Appearing In-Game
items.description: Rapper Kodak Black has been confirmed to be featured as an NPC in GTA 6 via a new batch of screenshots.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rapper Kodak Black has been confirmed to be featured as an NPC in GTA 6 via a new batch of screenshots.

Rockstar Games released a batch of 39 new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch, and one of them reveals that Kodak Black will be in the game. Upon closer examination, we can see him holding a cup with the Jack of Hearts logo, which is a club in GTA 6. This club has appeared in various marketing beats for the game, and Travis Scott even name-dropped it in his song, RHYNO, which was made specifically for GTA 6's soundtrack.

It has been heavily speculated that this club would feature a variety of real-world artists, and the confirmation of Kodak Black seems to only add fuel to that speculation. It doesn't seem like a leap to imagine that other artists like Scott or other rappers featured on the game's soundtrack could also appear in-game. There's some precedent for this in previous GTA titles, too.

In GTA Online, Dr Dre appeared as a character that the player could do missions for. The game's nightclubs also featured real DJs such as Solomun, Tale of Us, and Dixon, so it's entirely possible Rockstar managed to get these artists to do real performances at clubs in the game. We'll ultimately have to wait and see, but it's clear that Rockstar has spared no expense with the talent for this game. While there will be some fresh faces in the cast, actor Stephen Root confirmed earlier this year that he will play Brian Heder in GTA 6. The character is expected to be Jason's boss and a drug runner.

Some of the game's radio stations are also hosted by the likes of Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny, Morgan Wallen, and other major musicians and celebrities. There may be other celebrity cameos in GTA 6, but Rockstar is trying to keep a veil of secrecy around the entire game to preserve the experience for launch.

Speaking of launch, Rockstar Games confirmed earlier this week that pre-loading for GTA 6 will begin on November 10. The game will take up around 212 GBs of space on your storage device, so you may want to go clear some space for this behemoth so you have all the time needed to prepare for launch.

items.title: World of Warcraft Forever's Launch Was Running on Over 200,000 Gigabytes of RAM
items.description: World of Warcraft Forever launched last night, and while there were a ton of people playing, the servers were remarkably stable. And, it turns out that Blizzard dedicated a ton of resources to making those servers stable.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever launched last night, and while there were a ton of people playing, the servers were remarkably stable. It turns out that Blizzard dedicated a ton of resources to making sure those servers were solid.

Last night, after the game launched, Blizzard tweeted out a meme from its World of Warcraft account, with a Gnome tapping a car with the WoW Forever logo, with a caption saying: "*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever* This baby is running on: 3,924 Virtual Machines, 251,136 GB of Memory, 70,480 CPU Cores." That's a huge amount of memory, and it seems to have paid off with the smoothest Blizzard launch I've seen in years.

Blizzard's post bragging about the sheer amount of memory in its servers comes just a week after Sam Altman said in a podcast that it was "quite terrible" for people to have RAM in their own computers, rather than in a data center. Of course, he did later walk it back, instead claiming that he had "been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time." Still, that's 251,136GB of RAM that's dedicated to running an incredible MMO, rather than powering yet another data center.

*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever*
This baby is running on:
3,924 Virtual Machines
251,136 GB of Memory
70,480 CPU Cores https://t.co/P9PdRBzke7

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) November 5, 2026

Blizzard Executive Producer and Vice President for World of Warcraft Holly Longdale also posted celebrating the smooth launch, and said "this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built plans and contingencies. They are incredible imo." And, while we likely will never know just how many people logged into Forever for the launch, I can say firsthand that there were hundreds of characters in the starting zone right at 6pm EST, so the team definitely deserves recognition for holding everything together.

Even on the WoW forums, which are hardly a bastion of positivity, there are a number of threads with players praising WoW Forever for being one of the smoothest WoW launches of all time. On X/Twitter, WoW streamer Darth Microtransaction posted, "I don’t know how they did it, but they did. World of Warcraft Forever launch was the smoothest launch I’ve seen. Almost 0 Que[ue]. 0 dc, and no lag."

This launch was a solid start to a game that's going to take most people weeks to go through. The beta was huge on its own, despite being limited to just level 30. And, even when folks knew their characters would get deleted, so many people played the beta that developers commented on it for being the "craziest numbers [they've] seen." And now that the full game is here, it's going to be interesting to see what players discover, and what gets added in the future. Because, according to Blizzard, there's potential to visit some fan favorite locations from future expansions, too.

items.title: Microsoft Updates Xbox PC App, Says It's 60% Faster
items.description: Microsoft has updated the Xbox PC app so it’s faster and simpler, it said.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has updated the Xbox PC app so it’s faster and simpler, it said.

The Xbox PC app, available on PC, web, and cloud, launches up to 60% faster and makes it easier to find games, Jason Beaumont, VP, Xbox Experiences, said in a blog post. The changes are being rolled out to Xbox Insiders first, before wider availability.

Specifically, pages like Home, Store, and Game Pass load up to 50% faster, and in-app windows open up to 65% faster. But it’s worth noting that these results are based on Microsoft’s internal testing, and may be different for you depending on your device and internet connection.

We’re making XBOX on Windows faster and more responsive. Starting today, we’re rolling out updates that make our app up to 60% faster. A meaningful improvement, with plenty more to do. https://t.co/h5kzHSpR8H

— ASHA (@asha_shar) November 5, 2026

As for making it easier to find and play games, your cloud games are in one place, there’s more room to browse on larger screens (particularly helpful for desktop mode on PCs and larger displays), and the ability to choose between dark and light modes.

Elsewhere, Microsoft is bringing the refreshed look of the Xbox PC app to Xbox cloud gaming apps on supported TVs and VR headsets.

“These updates are another step toward making Xbox easier to use, more responsive, and more familiar wherever you choose to play,” Beaumont said. “We’ll continue listening to player feedback and improving over time.”

The Xbox PC app is in direct competition with the likes of Steam and the Epic Games Store for the hearts and minds of PC gamers, but I have all three (and a few more!) installed on my gaming computer. As a Game Pass Ultimate subscriber, I use the Xbox PC app mostly to play new games that are added to the service, or to find new family friendly games for my kids to play — preferably across multiple devices. Microsoft said the updated app will have an easier-to-use library, with simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organize games. Assuming this does indeed make it easier to browse your collection and find what you want to play, it’ll go down well in my household.

Similarly, the app has better search now, letting you search results across games, including installed titles and add-ons. And friends and social features are now part of the main navigation, making it easier to see what friends are playing, start a chat, or join a party. And finally, refreshed game cards, Home, Settings, and animations should make the app easier to scan and navigate.

Valve's Steam is the clear leader when it comes to PC gaming, and it seems there's little Microsoft or Epic can do to catch up. In Epic's case, it's thrown millions of dollars at the Epic Games Store (accessed via a recently refreshed launcher), in a bid to make a dent in Valve's dominance, but profitability continues to elude it. Microsoft has said it's seen growth in PC gaming at a time when its console business has struggled, so it makes sense to put some weight behind faster and more meaningful updates to the Xbox PC app.

items.title: Japanese News Show Features Drinkable Street Fighter Trading Cards
items.description: A Japanese news show claims it’s found the next popular thing in Japan: drinkable Street Fighter 6 trading cards. Each card contains a shot of energy, 12ml to be precise, and features designs from Capcom’s fighting game roster.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
A Japanese news show claims it’s found the next popular thing in Japan: drinkable Street Fighter 6 trading cards. Each card contains a shot of energy, 12ml to be precise, and features designs from Capcom’s fighting game roster.

You simply fold one of the cards in half, which is a statement that would usually make a card collector wince, and sup the little juice droplet from the center. The cards are called Energy Arts and the news clip showed designs for Ryu, E. Honda, Dhalsim, Jamie, and Vega. Here’s the clip:

A Japanese news show featured drinkable trading cards in its ranking of possible hit products for 2027.
Each card contains 12ml of an energy drink and the card/drink company already has a collab with Capcom's Street Fighter. https://t.co/XufheWvDvB

— Jeffrey J. Hall 🇯🇵🇺🇸 (@mrjeffu) November 4, 2026

The news channel predicted that the product will be a big thing in Japan in 2027. According to the show’s ranking, the Energy Arts cards come in fifth, behind this mysterious collection of odd names: Human Certificate, Fresh Food Crane Game, Muse Charm, and Edible Cactus “Sabo-Vege.”

Energy Arts cards were originally announced earlier in the year. The official press release said there are 24 cards to collect, and the idea behind the product was to “overturn the conventional idea of drinking” with what it called a “smart replenishment.”

It was created with esports players in mind, letting them get in a little sustenance and energy between rounds without taking time out for things like “drinking” a bottle of water.

“Whether you're playing a game, taking an exam, attending a meeting, or driving — in situations where concentration is required, the fact that refueling = interruption of concentration is a challenge for many people,” said the press release.

Instead of relying on caffeine like most energy drinks, the formula is built around what the company calls “fast-acting amino acids.” Apparently, the small quantity of juice inside cuts down on “the toilet problem,” because your bladder will probably barely register it.

You can leave the cards unsupped for 18 months before the drink inside turns bad. I don’t know what the process is for keeping them as a collectible if you don’t want to bend them or unseal them in any way.

items.title: Jason Momoa Reflects on Getting Beat Up by Timothée Chalamet in Dune: Part 3
items.description: Jason Momoa, if you hadn't noticed, is a much bigger man than Timothée Chalamet. In Dune: Part 3, however, size doesn’t matter.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Jason Momoa, if you hadn't noticed, is a much bigger man than Timothée Chalamet. In Dune: Part 3, however, size doesn’t matter.

Chalamet plays Paul Atreides in Dune: Part 3, which takes place 20 years after the events of the previous movie. Atreides is well established as the most powerful being in the universe, a messianic, totalitarian leader who can stab people real good.

Momoa kind of returns as a clone of his previous character from Dune: Part 1, Duncan Idaho, who doesn’t share any of his DNA dad’s memories or personality traits. “It’s probably the weirdest character I’ve ever had to navigate, because I know I was hired to play Duncan for a certain reason, then I had to figure out how to play a guy who doesn’t know who the guy is,” Momoa said in an interview with NY Times.

“It was very challenging. I’m not the most subtle actor, or human, so it was probably my most subtle performance. I haven’t seen it yet. I don’t know which takes he used.”

While Idaho and Atreides were close friends in Part 1, there’s more of a strain to that relationship in Part 3 and the pair come to blows. According to Momoa, it was challenging to wrap his head around the logistics of losing to Chalamet.

“And another thing too, working with Tim, I have to fight him,” Momoa explained. “[His character Paul] is at a whole other level, and better than me as a fighter. And you know, realistically, how do we put that together?”

Chalamet cut in to say that was “a polite way of putting” that Momoa could take him in a fight in real life. “He’s a better actor,” Momoa said. “I’m better at fighting. But he’s really fast. I was super impressed: Just because you’re a great actor, it doesn’t mean that you’re able to dance. Ultimately, it’s a dance.”

Elsewhere in the lead up to launch, we’ve had a look at Dune: Part 3’s horrific popcorn buckets. One comes with two sandworm holes for double the fun, and the other comes with a thumper that actually moves up and down.

Dune: Part 2 surpassed the previous movie in the trilogy at the box office, generating almost $500 million. Dune: Part 1 grossed $433 million worldwide during its entire theatrical run. Dune: Part 3 is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 18, 2026, with early IMAX preview screenings beginning on December 14, 2026.

Momoa kind of returns as a clone of his previous character from Dune: Part 1, Duncan Idaho, who doesn’t share any of his DNA dad’s memories or personality traits. “It’s probably the weirdest character I’ve ever had to navigate, because I know I was hired to play Duncan for a certain reason, then I had to figure out how to play a guy who doesn’t know who the guy is,” Momoa said in an interview with NY Times.

“It was very challenging. I’m not the most subtle actor, or human, so it was probably my most subtle performance. I haven’t seen it yet. I don’t know which takes he used.”

While Idaho and Atreides were close friends in Part 1, there’s more of a strain to that relationship in Part 3 and the pair come to blows. According to Momoa, it was challenging to wrap his head around the logistics of losing to Chalamet.

“And another thing too, working with Tim, I have to fight him,” Momoa explained. “[His character Paul] is at a whole other level, and better than me as a fighter. And you know, realistically, how do we put that together?”

Chalamet cut in to say that was “a polite way of putting” that Momoa could take him in a fight in real life. “He’s a better actor,” Momoa said. “I’m better at fighting. But he’s really fast. I was super impressed: Just because you’re a great actor, it doesn’t mean that you’re able to dance. Ultimately, it’s a dance.”

Elsewhere in the lead up to launch, we’ve had a look at Dune: Part 3’s horrific popcorn buckets. One comes with two sandworm holes for double the fun, and the other comes with a thumper that actually moves up and down.

Dune: Part 2 surpassed the previous movie in the trilogy at the box office, generating almost $500 million. Dune: Part 1 grossed $433 million worldwide during its entire theatrical run. Dune: Part 3 is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 18, 2026, with early IMAX preview screenings beginning on December 14, 2026.

items.title: Rockstar Games Releases 39 New GTA 6 Screenshots to Celebrate Two Weeks from Launch
items.description: Rockstar Games has released a few dozen new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games has released a few dozen new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch.

After 13 years of waiting, GTA 6 is finally almost here. The game is exactly 14 days away from release in the United States, and fans are eager to be able to visit Vice City once again. To help make the wait a bit more bearable, Rockstar has dropped 39 new screenshots from the game, which give us new looks at Vice City, the people within it, strip clubs, and some of the rip-roaring crimes that Jason and Lucia will take part in.

Rockstar Games released what is expected to be the final trailer for GTA 6 last month, which has been airing on TV constantly since its debut online. The game's marketing is also hard to ignore, as cities around the world have been covered in billboards, posters, and bus decals. Rockstar has gone all-out in the city of Miami by taking over the Miami Heat arena with GTA branding, selling in-universe beers from the games at bars, and flying a Vice City blimp around the city. Rockstar has essentially turned Miami into Vice City in real life, flexing the game's cultural power.

On November 18, Rockstar will also host a special event it calls "A Night in Vice City," which will feature a special NBA game between the Miami Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks. The Heat will be turned into the Vice City Heat and sport GTA-themed jerseys, while also playing on a new court. It's unclear if there will be other events in the city, but it wouldn't be surprising. Miami's nightclubs have also been turned into the GTA clubs over the last couple of weeks, showing a total takeover from Rockstar.

GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Pre-loading will begin on November 10 and will take up 212 GBs of space on your storage device. The game has already racked up an estimated $750 million in pre-orders, suggesting it will break an absurd amount of records once the floodgates open on release weekend.

items.title: Sony Announces Official Marvel's Wolverine Sales Figure for the First Time, Raises PlayStation Sales Forecast With GTA 6 Imminent
items.description: Sony has raised its sales forecast for its gaming business, while announcing an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine for the first time.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Sony has raised its sales forecast for its gaming business, while announcing an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine for the first time.

Sony said it had raised the sales forecast for its Game & Network Services Segment, which includes PlayStation, by 6% due to an “increase in sales of non-first-party game software titles.” Similarly, Sony raised the profit forecast for its gaming business by 6%, also citing the impact of an increase in sales of non-first-party games, but adding in an improvement in costs, and the impact of sales from network services (PlayStation Plus, etc).

Now, we all know what Sony is talking about here, or at least what it is mostly talking about: Grand Theft Auto 6. Sony’s partnership with Rockstar Games for GTA 6 has seen the PS5 at the forefront of the game’s marketing, so much so that the casual observer might not even know the game is also coming to Xbox Series X and S. Gameplay shown so far is from PS5 only, and marketing material says GTA 6 “plays best on PS5.”

Dragging profits down during the forecast for the current financial year, which ends March 31, 2027, is the delay to Sony Santa Monica’s God of War Laufey from February to May. But with GTA 6 set to become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, Sony will no doubt be comfortable with the sales shift into its next financial year.

Meanwhile, Sony said Marvel’s Wolverine sales had exceeded 2.4 million units. That’s as of November 4 — or 50 days after launch. To put that into context, fellow PS5 exclusive Ghost of Yotei sold 3.3 million units in 32 days, or just over a month after going on sale in October last year. Astro Bot had sold 1.5 million copies 58 days after going on sale in 2024.

Marvel’s Wolverine is well behind Insomniac’s previous game, Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, which sold a huge 2.5 million on day one (October 2023), 5 million just 11 days after launch, and 10 million after 107 days. The big question for Wolverine will be how well it continues to sell, with the crucial holiday season coming up.

Here’s what Sony had to say about Wolverine today:

“Regarding first-party titles, cumulative sales of Marvel’s Wolverine, released in September, exceeded 2.4 million units, contributing to the improved results of the entire segment for the quarter. We leveraged our expertise building the Marvel’s Spider-Man franchise to create a differentiated action game experience for Marvel’s Wolverine. Users have praised the new title for its highly immersive action, high-quality production, and richly layered storytelling.”

PS5 sales continue to decline, as Sony had said they would at this stage of the console’s lifecycle, but the company insisted “the PS platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner.”

And there was a brief note on its plans for the next generation of hardware, which is expected to involve a PS6 and possibly a handheld. “Looking ahead to next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetization through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next generation platform.”

Other notable financial results include the number of monthly active users (MAUs) across the PlayStation platform increasing 7% in September compared to the same month of the previous fiscal year to 127 million accounts — that’s a record high for September. Sony said this indicates “the baseline of engagement is steadily improving.”

Sony has of course raised the price of PS5 in response to memory scarcity fueled by the AI boom, but it downplayed the impact on its bottom line. “With regard to PlayStation (PS5) hardware, we have been able to offset the rise in memory prices through adjustments to promotions and pricing, as well as additional cost-reduction, and we expect hardware profitability for the current fiscal year to remain on par with the previous fiscal year,” it said.

“Regarding memory procurement for next fiscal year, based on discussions held so far with various suppliers, we have aligned on the quantity of memory needed for our projected hardware unit sales,” it continued.

items.title: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
items.description: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.

According to Bloomberg, operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion ‌yen (approx. $467 million) during the three months to September 30, off the back of a 15% decline in sales. CNBC said Nintendo sold 2.67 million Switch 2 units in the quarter, down 41% from the same period last year and down from the 3.82 million units that were sold during the first quarter of the current financial year (April to June 2026). Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 in September, fueled by the ongoing ‘RAMpocalypse’ that has also seen Microsoft and Sony raise the price of their consoles.

Despite this, Reuters reported that Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa insisted Nintendo had enough memory to meet its forecasted Switch 2 sales of 16.5 million units for the financial year ending March 2027, and is not considering further price changes.

Nintendo launches the Ocarina of Time remake today, and investors are hoping it will boost sales of the Switch 2 during the holiday sales season. Reuters said that investors remain concerned that the memory situation, as well as a “lack of high-profile titles” for Switch 2 this year, could negatively affect the console's momentum.

Nintendo's financial report reveals data for the first half of the current financial year, (from April to September 2026). During that six month period, Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 units, down from the 10.36 million it sold during the same period last year.

But there's important context to note here. Lifetime sales of the Switch 2 are now 26.35 million, which means it’s still outpacing the original Switch in terms of launch aligned sales (the first six quarters after release). It’s also worth noting that the Switch 2 enjoyed a record-breaking launch, fueled by ample stock availability, that saw it become the fastest-selling console of all time, so it was always going to be up against tough comparisons during its second year.

And countering apparent concern from investors, shares in Nintendo jumped 8.13% today following the release of the Ocarina of Time remake and the company's financial report.

As for video game sales, Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream sold 8.81 million units, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million units, and Splatoon Raiders sold 2.42 million units. Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the Switch 2 last year, “continued to sell steadily,” Nintendo said, shifting a further 1.78 million units during the two quarters.

Elsewhere, StarFox, released in June, sold 1.17 million units, and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, released in September, sold 1.34 million units. The expectation is that Nintendo will have some big hitters for Switch 2 in 2027, including, fans hope, the next mainline Super Mario game. Pokémon Winds & Pokémon Waves are confirmed for next year.

“Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina Of Time remake," Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games, told CNBC. "It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is.

“It’s getting harder and harder to sell video game hardware these days, and only hits help. Nintendo must step on the gas and deliver more big games next fiscal year to make sure the Switch 2 momentum continues.”
